name: Ahinoam
overview: Ahinoam appears in Scripture as a significant woman in the lives of two key Old Testament kings. She is first identified as the wife of King Saul, grounding her in the royal household of Israel (1 Samuel 14:50). Later, she is also named as one of King David's wives, specifically noted as Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and the mother of David’s firstborn, Amnon (1 Samuel 25:43; 1 Samuel 27:3; 2 Samuel 3:2). Her presence alongside Abigail during David’s time of trial and restoration highlights the personal and familial dimensions of David’s kingship (1 Samuel 30:5, 18). Thus, Ahinoam’s story reflects the intertwining of God’s providence in the lineage and legacy of Israel’s monarchy.
